beats: Retired, with income over ninety-five thousand? Part of your Old Age Security can go back to the government.
The OAS recovery tax takes fifteen cents of every dollar of net income above ninety-five thousand, three hundred and twenty-three.
Say your net income is one hundred and ten thousand. That's fourteen thousand, six hundred and seventy-seven over the line. Fifteen percent is two thousand, two hundred and one dollars.
It's repaid from your OAS payments, from July twenty twenty-seven to June twenty twenty-eight, based on your twenty twenty-six income.
Three legal levers. First, from age sixty-five, split up to half of your eligible pension income with your spouse.
Second, TFSA withdrawals aren't income. Third, delay your OAS: six-tenths of a percent for each month past sixty-five, up to thirty-six percent at seventy.
